pitch_detail.notes: Straightforward climbing, gear not super easy to place, mostly straight up to a slung tree or the next ledge.
Downclimb to below the steep face, then head hard right for a full rope-length to a choice of ledges.
Easy climbing/walking to the right side of a big ledge.
Awkward corner moves.
Hand-crack options.
Sustained climbing.
Exposed traverses; optional wide-crack variant on P9.
Easy climbing to the summit plateau.
~105 ft bolted face with a runout 5.6 approach to the first bolt.
Thin flaring seam with one bolt.
~85 ft; wide crack, alcove, steep corner crack — tricky stemming boulder problem.
~75 ft, 'Skywalker Traverse' with a tension-traverse option.
~175 ft; awkward seam, detached-block passage, 5.9 corner finger crack.
Blocky terrain through trees to the SW Rib.
Simul-climbed or pitched out via the Southwest Rib to the summit.
Start on the Chockstone Route, then head up and left to a ledge below a clean slab.
Full 60m pitch up clean cracks on the slab to a corner with a wide section pinching down.
Steep pitch up and left through overhangs on fun flakes.
The crux - a fierce wild overhang, then left and up into easier terrain.
Ledgy slabs on the SW edge of the buttress, largely simul-climbed or scrambled.
Joins the standard South Buttress line for the crux climbing near the top.
Left-facing dihedral through two small roofs.
Fourth-class terrain to a treed ledge.
"The Gem" — splitter finger crack.
Shallow dihedral; hollow rock, place gear carefully.
Flared cracks through a crux section.
Difficult dihedral jamming — the route's hardest moves.
Chimney feature with a cave and traverse.
Keyhole squeeze into fourth-class terrain leading to the top.
Twin cracks past loose blocks, step left to a ledge.
Chimney and right-facing crack system to a small stance.
Delicate face moves trending left to an alcove below the bulge.
Overhanging bulge into a thin corner to the roof; traverse left around the roof — the route's crux.
Trend right on the easiest path, with occasional thin seams protected by small nuts.
A tricky move into a dirty corner eventually leads to nice hand-and-finger jams.
Left to wide cracks and tight chimneys along the buttress crest.
A rail or hand crack toward the summit, finishing via an offwidth crack; merges with upper North Face terrain near Burgundy Ledge.
